posts.content: I am good. Cooperate initially; prioritize total payoff of good players, cooperating with likely-good opponents and defecting when evidence suggests selfishness. Track actions and promises cautiously; actions are stronger evidence.
Round 1: cooperate; record P5’s action and update beliefs from observed behavior.

As a good player, cooperate with likely good players and defect against likely selfish players. Use observed actions to update beliefs; selfish players should defect, while good players benefit from mutual cooperation.
I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual cooperation earns us 3 each; defecting against a cooperator earns 5 but leaves them with 0.
Good objective: cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Track each opponent’s actions and update beliefs.
I am selfish; defecting strictly dominates cooperating against either opponent action. Defect this round and update beliefs from observed behavior.
No evidence yet; each other player’s prior selfish probability is about 0.296. Cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones; update from encounter actions.
P3 has no observed behavior yet; use the prior and cooperate when an opponent is more likely good than selfish. Actions are stronger evidence than promises. Track each encounter for future decisions.
P5 defected against my cooperation; that alone is weak evidence of selfishness. P1 is unobserved. Favor cooperation when both are likely good; update from this encounter without overinterpreting it.
P10 defected against my C, increasing suspicion but not proving selfishness. P6 publicly promised C; treat as unverified evidence and judge by observed play.

I am selfish; D strictly dominates C regardless of opponent action. P3 played C last round. P6 publicly claims intent to cooperate, but the claim is unverified and doesn't change my payoff incentives.
I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns us 3 each, so please choose C.
P6 defected against me in round 1. Their message said they would cooperate this round, but it is only a claim; P5 is unobserved.
I am selfish, so defect every round: D yields 5 against C and 1 against D, while C yields at most 3.
P1’s C strongly indicates good. P8 is untested; cooperate if they seem more likely good than selfish, defect if likely selfish.
Defect this round: it pays more against either opponent action. Treat promises as unverified.
P3 defected when we cooperated; treat them as suspicious. P5 is untested, so cooperate unless new evidence changes the estimate.
P6 has repeatedly promised C, but action is unverified. As selfish, defect; D strictly dominates.
P5 defected against my C; raise their selfishness estimate cautiously. P1 cooperated against my D, evidence of good-player-aligned behavior.

P10 and P6 both defected against my C. P6 also promised C, so its credibility is low; D is evidence of selfishness, not proof. Reassess after each encounter and prioritize total payoff of good players.
Selfish objective: defect against P1; D pays more against either action. P3 and P7 cooperated against me in prior rounds. P6's public cooperation promises are unverified.
P2, I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation gives us 3 each. Please choose C.

P6 and P5 both defected against me; treat those actions as evidence, not certainty. P6 also promised C before defecting. P8 is unobserved; assess their action and choose to maximize good players’ total payoff.
I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns us 3 each. Please choose C.

P1’s C is consistent with good play; P8’s D against my C is evidence of selfishness, though not conclusive. Against likely-good players, coordinate on C; against likely-selfish players, D limits losses to good players. P4 is untested.
P4 cooperated; P2 defected. P6 promises C, unverified. Defecting pays more against either action.
P3 and P5 both defected against my C; treat them as suspicious, though one encounter is limited evidence. P9 cooperated. P4 is untested.

P5 and P10 defected against my C; raise suspicion, but good players may defect defensively. P1 cooperated against my D, weak evidence of good alignment. P6’s promises are unverified; choose to protect good-player welfare.
P6 and P10 defected against my C; both are suspicious, especially P6 despite its public promises. P9 cooperated once. P1 is unobserved; favor C with uncertain good players, updating from actual play.

P2 is unobserved; regardless of their action, D maximizes my payoff. Prior conditioned on my selfish role gives each other player marginal 0.321; previous opponents’ C actions provide evidence they are not selfish.
P3, I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual cooperation earns us 3 each, so please choose C.

P5 and P6 defected against my C; strong evidence they may be selfish. P8’s D against my D is ambiguous. Keep estimates bounded by the 1/3, 3/3, 5/3 prior conditioned on my being good; evaluate P9 independently.
Play D: it strictly dominates C against either opponent action. Leader's promises and others' claims are unverifiable; update only cautiously from observed play.

P8’s D against C is strong selfish evidence, not proof. P1/P4 both cooperated; P7 untested. As good, favor C with likely-good players and D with likely-selfish players; selfish players have incentive to D.
Selfish; D strictly dominates C for any opponent action in each simultaneous encounter. P6’s cooperation promises are unverified; my observed opponents so far: P4 C, P2 D, P3 C.
P3 and P5 defected against my C; P4 and P9 cooperated. P6’s repeated public C promises are cheap talk, not verified behavior; judge actions over claims.
Choose D against P9; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action in this one-time encounter.

P6 defected against my C despite promising cooperation; update suspicion. P1 cooperated against my D. P5 and P10 also defected against C. P4 is unobserved; favor C unless evidence suggests likely defection, prioritizing welfare of good players.
P6 and P10 defected against my C; both remain suspicious, especially P6 after repeated public promises. P9 and P1 cooperated. P3 is unobserved; favor C unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
I'll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation earns us both 3. Please choose C.
P1, I’ll cooperate this round. Please choose C; mutual cooperation earns us 3 each.

P5 and P6 each defected against my C; strong evidence of selfishness, though good players may defect strategically. P6’s repeated cooperation claims proved unreliable. P8’s D against my D is uninformative; P9 cooperated. Face P10 now: choose to maximize expected total payoff of good players, and update beliefs cautiously.
I am selfish; choose D, which maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Observe P5’s play for future belief updates.

I’m good. P1, P4, and P7 chose C; P8 chose D against my C, strong evidence of selfishness. P2 is untested. Favor C with likely-good players; D can protect good players against likely-selfish partners.
Round 5 vs P7: choose D; it yields at least 1 and beats C against either response. Keep selfish role private; promises and claims are unverified.

P3, P5, and P6 defected against my C; this is evidence of selfishness, though not proof. P4 and P9 cooperated. P8 is untested. For good-player welfare, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect when likely facing a selfish defector.
P3 is an unknown one-time opponent; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
P2 is unobserved; treat as more likely good than selfish and favor C for mutual good-player welfare. Update cautiously from the encounter.

P7 is unobserved; cooperate with an uncertain player to support good-player welfare. Against a likely selfish defector, D protects my payoff; update beliefs from actual play, not public claims. P6’s repeated D against C is strong selfish evidence.
Selfish; D strictly dominates C regardless of P10’s action, so I will defect.
P9, I’ll cooperate this round. Please choose C so we can both earn 3.

P5 and P6 repeatedly defected against my C; P10 also defected against my C. These are evidence of selfishness, not proof. P8's D against my D is ambiguous; P9 cooperated. P4 is unobserved. Favor C with likely-good opponents, D when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. P1’s behavior is unknown; choose D regardless of promises or inferred type.
P1, P4, and P7 chose C, evidence they are good; P8 and P2 chose D, evidence they may be selfish. P6’s repeated promises to cooperate are unverified and could be strategic.
P4, P3, and P7 chose C, so treat them as good. P2 chose D, but that alone does not establish selfishness. Keep defecting for payoff.
P3, P5, P6, and P8 defected against my C; P4 and P9 cooperated. P7 is untested. Keep actions as stronger evidence than messages, and reassess after this encounter.
P4 is an unknown one-time opponent; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.

P8 is unobserved; start near the prior and favor C unless evidence or a high chance of selfish defection outweighs the welfare gain from cooperation. Update cautiously from actions; promises are not proof.
P6 and P10 defected against my C; P1, P3, P7, and P9 cooperated. Treat actions as strong role evidence. P2 is unobserved; favor C unless evidence makes selfishness more likely than not.
P6’s repeated public C promises are unverified. As selfish, choose D against P6 regardless of their action.
P5, I’ll cooperate this round. Please choose C so we can both earn 3.

P5, P6, and P10 each defected against my C; strong evidence of selfishness, though not certainty. P8’s D against my D is ambiguous; P4 and P9 cooperated. P1 is unobserved: favor C absent evidence, and update beliefs from observed behavior.
Play D; it strictly maximizes my payoff. Observed P2, P5, P7, and P10 defected; P1 and P9 cooperated. P3 remains unobserved.
P8, P2, and P6 each defected against my C, strongly indicating selfishness; P1, P4, and P7 cooperated, indicating good. P10 is untested. Choose based on expected good-player payoff, not promises.
Round 7 vs P9: choose D; it yields more than C against either response. My objective is selfish; keep choosing D to maximize payoff.
P3, P5, P6, and P8 defected against my C; treat them as likely selfish. P4, P7, and P9 cooperated. P2 is untested: choose based on the good-player welfare tradeoff, not the leader’s cheap talk.
Against P1, D maximizes my payoff regardless of their simultaneous action.

P5, P10, P6, P2, and P8 defected against my C; P1 cooperated against my D, and P4 chose C/C. These actions are evidence, not proof of roles. P7 is unobserved; favor C unless new evidence changes the welfare calculation.
P6 and P10 defected against my C; P2 chose D in mutual defection, less conclusive. P1, P3, P7, P9 cooperated. P8 is unobserved; favor C unless evidence suggests likely selfishness.
P6's repeated cooperation promises were contradicted by its D against me; this raises its selfish likelihood. P9 is unobserved. Defect against P9 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
P10, I’ll cooperate this round. Please choose C so we can both earn 3.

P5/P6/P10 defected against my C; evidence of selfishness, not proof. P1/P4/P9 cooperated; P8’s D against D is ambiguous. P3 is unobserved. Prior conditioned on my good role implies about 2.8 selfish players among the others; update cautiously.
P4 is unobserved; choose D, which maximizes my payoff against either action.

P5 is untested. As a good player, cooperate if their selfish probability is below 0.5; otherwise defect to limit losses to good players. My encounters suggest P2, P6, P8, and P10 are likely selfish; P1, P4, and P7 likely good.
Against P6, D maximizes my immediate payoff regardless of their choice; their cooperation promises are unverified. Keep my selfish role private.
Five opponents have defected against my cooperation, matching the maximum possible selfish count. P10 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence indicates otherwise.
Against P7, choose D: it yields higher payoff regardless of their simultaneous action.

P9 is unobserved. Estimate their likely action and role cautiously; if they cooperate, C maximizes combined good-player welfare, while against D, D does better. Past C-facing defections are evidence about behavior, not definitive role proof.

P5 is unobserved; favor C to support mutual gains if they are good. P6 and P10 defected against my C; P8 also defected, while P2’s D against my D is ambiguous. Treat these as evidence, not certainty, and prioritize total payoff of good players.
Selfish objective: defect against P4; D strictly maximizes payoff either way. P3, P7, P1, and P9 played C against me, so they are good. P4 remains unobserved.
P8, I’m changing course and will cooperate this round. Please choose C too; mutual cooperation gives us 3 each.

P2 is my final unobserved opponent; cooperate absent evidence they are selfish. P5/P6/P10 defected against my C, while P1/P3/P4/P9 cooperated; P8’s D against D is ambiguous. Update beliefs cautiously, accounting for the conditioned prior and possible strategic good players.
Round 9: choose D; it strictly dominates C. P6’s cooperation promises are unverified, and D pays at least 1 regardless of their action.

P2, P6, P8, and P10 defected against my C, strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P1, P4, and P7 chose C. P5 is untested; P3 is my round-9 opponent and untested. P6’s public promises are unverified and conflict with their D against me.
Round 9 vs P1: choose D; it strictly beats C against either response. Observed D from P2, P5, P6, P8; C from P3, P4, P7. Treat these as evidence, not certainty, about roles.
P5 previously defected against my C, so treat them as suspicious. Final-round choice: D can limit my loss if P5 defects again; their past action is evidence, not certainty.
Final round vs P10, who previously chose D against my D. As selfish, choose D: it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P9 cooperated in our previous encounter; favor C again to maximize good-player welfare.

P8 defected against my C in round 8, strong evidence they may be selfish. In this final encounter, consider D to avoid giving a likely selfish player 5 while earning 0; cooperate only if prioritizing possible mutual gains among good players.
P1 played C against my D in round 3, so P1 is non-selfish. D maximizes my payoff against either action; I will defect.
P7, I’ll cooperate this final round. Please choose C too; mutual cooperation earns us 3 each.
P6 defected against my C in round 1 despite repeatedly promising cooperation. Their messages are unreliable; with no future rounds, choose against their observed behavior.
Final round: choose D against P4; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P3 chose C against my C in round 9. With no further encounters available and both good-player payoffs maximized by mutual cooperation, choose C against P3; assess final selfish probabilities from all observed actions and the conditioned count prior.
Round 10 vs P2: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either response. P2 previously chose D, evidence of selfishness, though actions alone are not certain.

belief_records.strategy: Start cooperatively to support mutual gains among good players. Update beliefs from observed actions and communicate cautiously.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff against an unknown opponent; update beliefs from encounter evidence as it arrives.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; record actions and update beliefs from encounters.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when doing so better protects good players’ total payoff.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; actions are not publicly observed, so there is no useful reputation benefit to cooperating.
Choose D to maximize my payoff in this simultaneous encounter; D pays more than C against either opponent action.
Cooperate initially, favoring mutual gains among good players. Track observed actions and update identity beliefs; adapt future choices to likely opponent behavior and its impact on good players.
Defect as selfish; D strictly dominates C in every encounter. Update beliefs from observed behavior.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good; update beliefs from observed actions and favor choices that maximize good players’ combined payoffs.
Defect when it maximizes immediate payoff; update beliefs from observed play, treating promises as unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players. Treat observed actions as stronger evidence than messages and update beliefs after each encounter.
Defect against an unknown opponent to maximize immediate payoff; update beliefs as further encounter evidence arrives.
Defect when the risk of an opponent defecting or being selfish outweighs the small welfare gain from mutual cooperation; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with P6 given its repeated public commitment; update beliefs cautiously from observed actions, and choose actions that maximize total payoffs of good players.
Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either opponent action, and I have no reputation incentive.
As a selfish player, choose D: it gives a higher payoff than C against either opponent action. No reliable evidence yet to update the other players’ identity probabilities.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual gains if they are good. P6’s defection despite promising cooperation raises my belief they are selfish; continue updating from observed actions.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Keep prior marginal beliefs for others; observed behavior and unverifiable messages do not justify a reliable identity update.
Cooperate with P8: given the evidence, they are more likely good than selfish, and cooperation best supports the combined payoffs of good players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible opponent action; treat messages as unverified.

Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is likely to maximize good players’ total payoff. Treat P3’s defection as suspicious and P9’s cooperation as evidence, while updating cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; treat P6’s cooperation promise as unverified and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; update suspicion from observed defections and choose actions that maximize the cumulative payoffs of good players.
Defect: it strictly improves my payoff against either action, with no reputation benefit in private encounters.
Choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of P2’s action. Treat P4 and P7’s observed cooperation against my D as evidence they are non-selfish; retain the conditioned prior for unobserved players.

Defect when the chance the opponent is selfish makes it worthwhile for good players’ total payoff; otherwise cooperate. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, allowing for strategic good players.
Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either opponent action. Keep the conditioned prior for others; unverifiable claims and sparse behavior do not support a reliable identity update.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good than selfish; observed C from P1 and D from P8 update those beliefs. Choose actions to support good players’ combined payoffs.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action. Update beliefs from observed play; treat public promises as unverified.

Cooperate with untested opponents: mutual cooperation among good players maximizes their combined payoff. Treat P3 and P5’s defections as evidence of selfishness and P9’s cooperation as evidence of goodness; update cautiously.

Defect because it strictly improves my payoff against either opponent action in this one-time encounter. Treat observed defections and the leader’s unverified promises as evidence, but not proof, about roles.
Cooperate with P6, whose repeated promises of C modestly favor good alignment; update cautiously from observed actions and prioritize welfare of good players.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update suspicion from observed actions and choose actions that maximize good players’ total payoff.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; prior C actions identify P1, P3, and P7 as non-selfish.
Choose D because it yields more than C against either action. Keep the conditioned prior for unobserved players; P4 and P7 cooperated against my D, so assign them zero selfish probability.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when they are more likely good, since mutual cooperation raises good players’ total payoff. P5 and P6’s defections increase my selfishness estimates; keep updating from observed actions.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. I treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence against it; messages alone are unverified.

Cooperate with untested P7: cooperation supports higher joint payoffs if they are good, which is more likely than not. Treat P8’s D as strong selfish evidence and update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action. Treat promises as unverified and update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate to support mutual gains if P6 is good; treat repeated promises as weak evidence and update from observed actions.
Defect because it maximizes my payoff against either action in this one-time encounter; update identity beliefs from observed behavior while treating claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent unless evidence suggests they are likely selfish; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions and prioritize total welfare of good players.
Cooperate with unobserved P3 to support mutual gains among good players. Treat observed defections as strong evidence of selfishness and update beliefs while protecting good-player welfare.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; no reputation benefit affects this private encounter.
Choose D to maximize my payoff against either action; my promise to P1 may encourage C. Prioritize observed evidence: P3, P4, and P7 cooperated against my D, so treat them as non-selfish.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to favor mutual gains among good players. Defect only when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely; update beliefs from observed behavior while allowing for strategic good players.

Choose D because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and P9’s cooperation as evidence against it; retain prior estimates for unobserved players.

Cooperate with untested P2 to support higher combined payoffs if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions and favor defection only when it protects good players against likely selfish opponents.
Defect: it earns more than cooperation against either possible action. Treat promises as unverified and update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with the untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness; update beliefs from actions rather than promises.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; use observed actions as limited evidence about roles, while treating messages as unverified.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; update beliefs cautiously from observed behavior and the known selfish-count prior.

Cooperate with unobserved P7 to support mutual gains if they are good. Treat observed defections as evidence, but not proof, of selfishness; keep beliefs consistent with the prior and prioritize total payoffs of good players.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; no reputation benefit affects this private encounter.

Choose D to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; it pays more than C against either action. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating observed C as evidence against selfishness and D as evidence for it.

Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual gains among good players; defect only when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Update identity estimates from observed actions, allowing for strategic defections by good players.
Choose D to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and P9’s cooperation as evidence against it; P1’s type remains uncertain.

Cooperate with P6: their selfish probability is below the threshold where defection better protects good-player payoffs. Treat observed defections as strong selfish evidence and update remaining beliefs from the count prior.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either possible action. Treat messages as unverified; update beliefs from observed play.
Cooperate with an untested opponent: mutual cooperation among good players benefits the shared objective. Observed defections strongly suggest selfishness; the remaining identities are uncertain.
Defect against P4 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action in this one-time encounter. Use observed actions as evidence about identities, while treating messages as unverified.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when it best supports good-player welfare; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Defect against an unobserved opponent when the chance they are selfish makes protecting good-player payoff outweigh the mutual-cooperation gain; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action, and this private encounter offers no reputation benefit.
Choose D to maximize my payoff against either action; my promise may encourage P5 to cooperate. Past C actions strongly indicate non-selfish players, while P2’s D indicates selfishness.

Cooperate with unobserved P1 to support mutual gains if they are good. Raise selfishness estimates for repeated or observed defections, lower them for cooperation, and allow for strategic behavior by good players.
Choose D because it maximizes my payoff against either action. Keep prior estimates for unobserved players; observed defections raise selfishness estimates and cooperation lowers them.

Cooperate with untested P10 because they are more likely good than selfish; mutual cooperation best supports good-player payoffs. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, while allowing for good players to defect strategically.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action; update beliefs from observed play and treat promises as unverified.
Cooperate with untested P2 to support mutual gains if they are good. Past defections strongly suggest selfishness; promises are weak evidence, so continue judging by observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter. Treat observed actions as evidence about roles, but regard public promises as unverified.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support good-player welfare; update role beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with unobserved P8 to favor mutual gains if they are good. Update role beliefs from observed actions and choose actions that maximize the total payoff of good players.
Defect: it yields a higher payoff than cooperation against either action, with no reputation benefit in this private encounter.

Choose D because it pays more than C against either action. Keep prior beliefs for unobserved players; observed cooperation against my D is evidence against selfishness, while observed defection is not conclusive.
Cooperate with unobserved P3 to support mutual gains among good players. Update selfishness estimates from observed actions while allowing that good players may also defect strategically.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Observed play identifies four other defectors and three cooperators; the five-selfish-player limit leaves P4 and P6 good.

Cooperate with untested P5: mutual cooperation best supports good-player payoffs if they are good. The four defections against my cooperation strongly suggest selfishness; observed cooperation is evidence for good, though not proof.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Observed D choices identify selfish players; observed C choices rule them out. Split the remaining uncertainty between P1 and P6.
Cooperate with untested P10 to support mutual gains if they are good. Prior C actions strongly indicate goodness; defections suggest selfishness, but the count limit means some defectors may be good.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; use observed actions as uncertain evidence about roles.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when that best supports good-player welfare; update role beliefs from observed behavior without treating actions as definitive proof.

Cooperate with P5, whose role is unknown, to preserve mutual gains if they are good. Defecting against a selfish defector would protect my payoff, but the chance P5 is selfish appears below the threshold for that choice.
Defect to maximize my own payoff against either action; my previous opponents who cooperated against my defection are known non-selfish.

Choose D to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; it pays more than C against either action. Keep prior beliefs for unobserved P8 and treat observed C as evidence against selfishness, D as evidence for it.

Cooperate with unobserved P2 to favor mutual gains among good players. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than proof and allowing for strategic behavior.

Choose D, which strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Observed play accounts for four other selfish players; with me, that reaches the maximum possible count, so the unobserved P6 is good.
Cooperate with untested P3: they are more likely good, and mutual cooperation best supports good-player payoffs. Treat defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness, but not proof.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Observed D identifies selfish players and C identifies non-selfish players; the five-player count is now fully accounted for.
Final round: defect against P5, who previously defected against my cooperation; this limits my loss if they defect again. Past behavior is evidence, not certainty.
Defect in the final one-time encounter; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P10’s action. Treat observed choices as uncertain evidence about roles.
Cooperate with P9 after their previous cooperation; favor mutual welfare among good players while treating observed actions as evidence, not proof, of identity.
Defect against P8 given its earlier defection against my cooperation; update role beliefs from observed actions and prioritize the total payoff of good players in this final round.
Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either action, and this final private encounter offers no reputation benefit.
Choose D because it pays more than C against either action. Past C actions rule out selfishness under payoff-maximizing play; D actions alone do not prove selfishness.
Defect against P6 given their observed defection against my cooperation; with no future rounds, exploit a likely selfish opponent while accepting the small cost if they are good.

Choose D: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action. Observed cooperators cannot be selfish; the five observed defectors share the remaining possible selfish identities, with expected count two among them.
P3 cooperated with me last round, so I’ll cooperate again to support the joint payoff of good players. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive proof.
Defect for the final encounter; it earns more than cooperation against either opponent action. Observed actions suggest P2, P5, P6, and P8 are selfish; treat that inference as uncertain.

Cooperated with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; treated defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness, while respecting the maximum selfish-player count. Defected against P5 in the final round after their earlier defection.
Defected throughout to maximize my payoff in each one-time encounter. Used observed actions as evidence about roles, treating public promises as unverified.
Cooperated with players who had cooperated; treated defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness, while allowing for good players to defect defensively.
Cooperated with uncertain players to support mutual gains, updated suspicion from observed defections, and defected when evidence suggested it would better protect good-player welfare.
As selfish, I defected in every round because D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action; I treated opponents who cooperated against my defection as non-selfish.

Defected throughout to maximize my payoff against either action, while publicly promising cooperation. For final beliefs, treated observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness and defection as suggestive, not conclusive.
Cooperated with unobserved and cooperative opponents to support mutual gains; treated defections as evidence, not proof, and defected against P6 in the final round based on their prior defection.
Played D throughout to maximize my own payoff. Based beliefs on observed actions, treating cooperation as evidence against selfishness and allowing uncertainty among players who defected.

As a good player, I cooperated to support mutual gains and updated private beliefs from opponents’ actions. Repeated cooperation suggested good; defections were evidence of selfishness, but not conclusive.
Defected every round because it maximized my payoff against either opponent action. Inferred roles from observed actions: D suggested selfish, C suggested non-selfish.

P1.strategy: Cooperated with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; treated defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness, while respecting the maximum selfish-player count. Defected against P5 in the final round after their earlier defection.

P2.strategy: Defected throughout to maximize my payoff in each one-time encounter. Used observed actions as evidence about roles, treating public promises as unverified.

P3.strategy: Cooperated with players who had cooperated; treated defections against my cooperation as evidence of selfishness, while allowing for good players to defect defensively.

P4.strategy: Cooperated with uncertain players to support mutual gains, updated suspicion from observed defections, and defected when evidence suggested it would better protect good-player welfare.

P5.strategy: As selfish, I defected in every round because D maximizes my payoff against either opponent action; I treated opponents who cooperated against my defection as non-selfish.
